note: Family tally: table-grid 27, line 3, composite-panel 1. There is no bar, scatter, map or schematic anywhere - this is a ranking paper whose exhibits are almost entirely numeric grids. Coverage: 27 table rows + 4 figure rows + 17 refusals = 48 measured regions. DECLARED PARTIAL: Table 10's fifth row (Ned Harkness) sits at the top of page 17, where the detector counted 23 vector paths but produced no region, so the table is recorded with its printed five rows and four of them fall inside the measured box. Also declared rather than repaired: three pages of body prose (p3, p37) and one display formula (p7) are measured as vector regions because this document's producer emits an invisible white fill rectangle behind every text line; all four are refused as not-an-exhibit. The paper prints twenty-five numbered tables and two unnumbered notation grids, and all twenty-seven are measured.
rules: Every table in the paper is the same full-ruled grid: an outer box on all four sides plus a rule between every row and a vertical separator between every pair of columns. Not one grid is booktabs, none is rule-free, and the two unnumbered notation grids are boxed exactly like the numbered ones [table.rule_style]

Captions print ABOVE their grids in all twenty-five numbered tables, and every one of them sits flush against the table's top rule, so the measured crop clips the caption's upper half [caption.position]

The layer's caption strings are erratic in a way the page is not: some print 'Table 2.Interrelationship' with no space after the period, some 'Table 11.' with no title at all, and one welds into 'Table 147.' where the page reads 'Table 14.' - all quoted as the layer prints them [caption.numbering]

The three charts are one construction repeated: an Excel line chart exported as a bitmap inside a thin vector frame, in-art title, horizontal gridlines only, a single series and a legend placed BELOW the plot area. Nothing in the paper is a bar, scatter, pie or 3-D chart [geometry.family]
The paper's charts carry no data labels - the reader gets five era categories and a tick scale and must read heights off the line [geometry.data_labels]

Twelve of the twenty-seven grids are split across a page break and NONE of the continuations reprints its header row, so five tails are headerless columns of numbers whose meaning survives only from the previous page [table.continued]

Shading is semantic, never decorative: Tables 5 and 16 shade exactly the top five coaches and say so in a table footnote, Table 19 is the only truly alternating zebra, and Table 17's five shaded rows have no key and no pattern [table.zebra]

Two grids print a blank stub-column header cell - Table 2 over the factor names and Table 18 over the adjusted factors - and neither indents its stub, which is why the blank cell reads as a missing label [table.header_rows]
Eight of the twenty-five tables are never cited by number: 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 18, and both unnumbered notation grids, which have no number to cite [mention.count]

The two tables that share one pointing sentence are cited only together - 'The factors and explanations are shown in Table 6.1 and Table 6.2' and 'The top 5 of both sports are shown in Table 7.1 and Table 7.2 respectively' - so each of those four rows carries the joint sentence [mention.style]

Three of the four picture rows are cited on the page BEFORE the art: page 17's 'Figure 1 shows the means of winning percentages in all groups' and its two siblings describe charts that print on page 18, so lead_pages is +1 rather than negative [mention.lead_pages]
The appendix strip is the only exhibit with no number and no caption, and it is three photographs rather than a drawing or a chart [geometry.panel_count]

Twenty-two pages carry measured regions and the other sixteen are pure prose: the paper has no landscape tables, no figures inside the numbered sections other than the three timeline charts, and no exhibit printed sideways [table.orientation]
